more_info.overview: Stearyl citrate is a mixture of mono-, di- and tristearyl esters of citric acid. It is manufactured by reacting citric acid with stearyl alcohol. FDA lists antioxidant, emulsifying, metal-binding and surface-active functions for the preparation. Specified applications include margarine, non-alcoholic beverages, fats and oils under manufacturing conditions.
more_info.origin: Manufactured by esterifying citric acid with stearyl alcohol. The synthetic reaction produces a mixture of mono-, di- and tristearyl citrate. The definition does not establish whether every commercial stearyl-alcohol feedstock is derived from plant or animal fat.
more_info.uses: FDA lists margarine, non-alcoholic beverages, fats and oils. The preparation has antioxidant, emulsifying, metal-binding and surface-active functions, with amounts governed by the stated manufacturing conditions.
